tagline: Go file sync and sharing platform in one container or binary, for a small server or Kubernetes.
description: ownCloud Infinite Scale, or oCIS, is a file sync and sharing server written in Go under the Apache 2.0 licence. You install it as one executable or one container. A small board such as a Raspberry Pi can host it, and the same code can later spread across a Kubernetes cluster once you adjust the settings and run more services. The README shows a Docker quickstart with an init step and a run step that listens on port 9200. Web, Android, iOS and desktop clients synchronise through WebDAV and CS3 APIs, and the web client lives in the same repository. Sign-in uses OpenID Connect, with either Keycloak or an embedded identity provider. Collaborative office editing is possible through Collabora Online, OnlyOffice or Microsoft Office Online Server, connected by a WOPI gateway. As a Dropbox Plus replacement it covers sync and sharing; the office suite is a separate component you must run. Some builds published by ownCloud GmbH fall under an end user licence agreement.
strengths: Single binary or container for small and large setups
Official web, Android, iOS and desktop clients
OpenID Connect sign-in with an embedded provider
Office editing via Collabora, OnlyOffice or Microsoft Office Online Server
limits: Document editing needs a separate office server connected through WOPI
Some stable builds from ownCloud GmbH are covered by an end user licence agreement
Multi-service architecture adds configuration work as you scale up
The README quickstart uses an insecure setting meant for evaluation only
bestFor: An organisation with an admin comfortable with Docker or Kubernetes that wants Dropbox-style sharing on its own infrastructure.
